sanskrit: anāthāṃ pramadāṃ bālāṃ vṛddhāṃ bhītāṃ tapasvinīm vañcayanti narā ye ca te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those men who deceive a helpless woman, a child, an old person, one in fear, or one given to austerity — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: vṛtticchedaṃ gṛhacchedaṃ dāracchedaṃ ca bhārata mitracchedaṃ tathāśāyās te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who cut off a man's livelihood, his home, his wife, his friend, or his very hope, O Bhārata — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: sūcakāḥ saṃdhibhettāraḥ paravṛttyupajīvakāḥ akṛtajñāś ca mitrāṇāṃ te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Informers, breakers of alliances, those who live by another's labor, and the ungrateful toward their friends — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: pāṣaṇḍā dūṣakāś caiva samayānāṃ ca dūṣakāḥ ye pratyavasitāś caiva te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Heretics, defilers, those who violate covenants, and those who have fallen back from their vows — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: kṛtāśaṃ kṛtanirveśaṃ kṛtabhaktaṃ kṛtaśramam bhedair ye vyapakarṣanti te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who, by sowing discord, draw away one who has placed his hope in them, who has served them, given his devotion, and spent his toil for them — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: paryaśnanti ca ye dārān agnibhṛtyātithīṃs tathā utsannapitṛdevejyās te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who eat before their wives, their servants, and their guests have eaten, and who have let the worship of the fathers and the gods lapse — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: vedavikrayiṇaś caiva vedānāṃ caiva dūṣakāḥ vedānāṃ lekhakāś caiva te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Sellers of the Vedas, defilers of the Vedas, and those who commit the Vedas to writing — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: cāturāśramyabāhyāś ca śrutibāhyāś ca ye narāḥ vikarmabhiś ca jīvanti te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those men who stand outside the four stages of life, outside the revealed scripture, and who live by forbidden acts — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: keśavikrayikā rājan viṣavikrayikāś ca ye kṣīravikrayikāś caiva te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Dealers in hair, O king, dealers in poison, and dealers in milk — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ caiva kanyānāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira ye 'ntaraṃ yānti kāryeṣu te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who, O Yudhiṣṭhira, slip in to obstruct the affairs of brāhmaṇas, of cattle, and of maidens — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: śastravikrayakāś caiva kartāraś ca yudhiṣṭhira śalyānāṃ dhanuṣāṃ caiva te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Sellers of weapons, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and the makers of barbed darts and of bows — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: śalyair vā śaṅkubhir vāpi śvabhrair vā bharatarṣabha ye mārgam anurundhanti te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who block the road with spikes, with stakes, or with pits, O bull of the Bharatas — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: upādhyāyāṃś ca bhṛtyāṃś ca bhaktāṃś ca bharatarṣabha ye tyajanty asamarthāṃs tāṃs te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who abandon their teachers, their servants, and their devoted dependents when these are helpless, O bull of the Bharatas — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: aprāptadamakāś caiva nāsānāṃ vedhakās tathā bandhakāś ca paśūnāṃ ye te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who break in beasts before their time, who pierce their noses, and who keep cattle in bondage — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: agoptāraś chaladravyā baliṣaḍbhāgatatparāḥ samarthāś cāpy adātāras te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who fail to protect, who gain their wealth by fraud, who are intent on exacting the sixth-part tribute, and who, though able, give nothing — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: kṣāntān dāntāṃs tathā prājñān dīrghakālaṃ sahoṣitān tyajanti kṛtakṛtyā ye te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those who, once their purpose is served, abandon the patient, the self-controlled, and the wise who have long dwelt with them — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: bālānām atha vṛddhānāṃ dāsānāṃ caiva ye narāḥ adattvā bhakṣayanty agre te vai nirayagāminaḥ
english: Those men who eat first, without first giving to the young, the old, and the servants — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

sanskrit: ete pūrvarṣibhir dṛṣṭāḥ proktā nirayagāminaḥ bhāginaḥ svargalokasya vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
english: These the ancient seers beheld and declared to be bound for hell. Now I shall tell you, O bull of the Bharatas, of those who share in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: sarveṣv eva tu kāryeṣu daivapūrveṣu bhārata hanti putrān paśūn kṛtsnān brāhmaṇātikramaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: In all undertakings that begin with rites to the gods, O Bhārata, an affront committed against a brāhmaṇa destroys one's sons and all one's cattle entirely.

sanskrit: dānena tapasā caiva satyena ca yudhiṣṭhira ye dharmam anuvartante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who, O Yudhiṣṭhira, follow the way of dharma through giving, through austerity, and through truth — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣābhis tapobhiś ca śrutam ādāya bhārata ye pratigrahaniḥsnehās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who, having gained sacred learning through service and austerity, O Bhārata, feel no craving to accept gifts — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: bhayāt pāpāt tathābādhād dāridryād vyādhidharṣaṇāt yatkṛte pratimucyante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those for whose sake others are delivered from fear, from sin, from oppression, from poverty, and from the ravages of disease — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: kṣamāvantaś ca dhīrāś ca dharmakāryeṣu cotthitāḥ maṅgalācārayuktāś ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: The forbearing and the steadfast, those ever roused to acts of dharma, and those devoted to auspicious conduct — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: nivṛttā madhumāṃsebhyaḥ paradārebhya eva ca nivṛttāś caiva madyebhyas te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who have turned away from honey and flesh, from the wives of others, and from intoxicating drink — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: āśramāṇāṃ ca kartāraḥ kulānāṃ caiva bhārata deśānāṃ nagarāṇāṃ ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: The founders of hermitages, of families, of regions, and of cities, O Bhārata — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: vastrābharaṇadātāro bhakṣapānānnadās tathā kuṭumbānāṃ ca dātāras te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who give garments and ornaments, food, drink, and victuals, and who provide for whole households — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: sarvahiṃsānivṛttāś ca narāḥ sarvasahāś ca ye sarvasyāśrayabhūtāś ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who have ceased from all harm, who endure all things, and who become a refuge for all — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva śuśrūṣanti jitendriyāḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ caiva sasnehās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who, masters of their senses, serve their mother and father, and bear affection toward their brothers — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: āḍhyāś ca balavantaś ca yauvanasthāś ca bhārata ye vai jitendriyā dhīrās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who, though wealthy, strong, and in the bloom of youth, O Bhārata, yet remain steadfast and masters of their senses — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: aparāddheṣu sasnehā mṛdavo mitravatsalāḥ ārādhanasukhāś cāpi te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who remain affectionate even toward offenders, who are gentle, fond of their friends, and easy to win over — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: sahasrapariveṣṭāras tathaiva ca sahasradāḥ trātāraś ca sahasrāṇāṃ puruṣāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who feast thousands, who give to thousands, and who are the protectors of thousands — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: suvarṇasya ca dātāro gavāṃ ca bharatarṣabha yānānāṃ vāhanānāṃ ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: The givers of gold and of cattle, O bull of the Bharatas, and of carriages and draught-animals — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: vaivāhikānāṃ kanyānāṃ preṣyāṇāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira dātāro vāsasāṃ caiva te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who give maidens in marriage, who give attendants and garments, O Yudhiṣṭhira — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: vihārāvasathodyānakūpārāmasabhāpradāḥ vaprāṇāṃ caiva kartāras te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who provide pleasure-grounds, resting-houses, gardens, wells, groves, and assembly-halls, and who build embankments — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: niveśanānāṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ vasatīnāṃ ca bhārata dātāraḥ prārthitānāṃ ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who give dwellings, fields, and lodgings, O Bhārata, and whatever is asked of them — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: rasānām atha bījānāṃ dhānyānāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira svayam utpādya dātāraḥ puruṣāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who, having themselves raised juices, seeds, and grain, O Yudhiṣṭhira, then give them away — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: yasmin kasmin kule jātā bahuputrāḥ śatāyuṣaḥ sānukrośā jitakrodhāḥ puruṣāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: In whatever family they are born, men blessed with many sons and a span of a hundred years, full of compassion and having conquered their wrath — they are bound for heaven.

sanskrit: etad uktam amutrārthaṃ daivaṃ pitryaṃ ca bhārata dharmādharmau ca dānasya yathā pūrvarṣibhiḥ kṛtau
english: Thus has it been told, for the sake of the world beyond, regarding the rites to the gods and to the fathers, O Bhārata, and the dharma and adharma of giving, even as the ancient seers ordained them.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca idaṃ me tattvato rājan vaktum arhasi bhārata ahiṃsayitvā keneha brahmahatyā vidhīyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This, O king, you ought to tell me truly, O Bhārata — by what act here, even without slaying, is the guilt of brahmin-murder incurred?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vyāsam āmantrya rājendra purā yat pṛṣṭavān aham tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: Bhīṣma said: That which I once asked of Vyāsa, having addressed him, O lord of kings, I shall now relate to you in full — listen here with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: caturthas tvaṃ vasiṣṭhasya tattvam ākhyāhi me mune ahiṃsayitvā keneha brahmahatyā vidhīyate
english: You who are the fourth in descent from Vasiṣṭha — declare to me the truth, O sage: by what act here, even without slaying, is the guilt of brahmin-murder incurred?

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭo mahārāja parāśaraśarīrajaḥ abravīn nipuṇo dharme niḥsaṃśayam anuttamam
english: Thus questioned, O great king, the son born of Parāśara's body, skilled in dharma, spoke without doubt and beyond all dispute.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ svayam āhūya bhikṣārthe kṛśavṛttinam brūyān nāstīti yaḥ paścāt taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who himself summons a brāhmaṇa of meager livelihood to receive alms, and afterward says, 'There is nothing' — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: madhyasthasyeha viprasya yo 'nūcānasya bhārata vṛttiṃ harati durbuddhis taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: The man of evil mind who robs of his livelihood a learned and impartial brāhmaṇa here, O Bhārata — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: gokulasya tṛṣārtasya jalārthe vasudhādhipa utpādayati yo vighnaṃ taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who, O lord of the earth, raises an obstacle to the water sought by a herd of cattle tormented by thirst — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yaḥ pravṛttāṃ śrutiṃ samyak śāstraṃ vā munibhiḥ kṛtam dūṣayaty anabhijñāya taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who, in his ignorance, reviles the established sacred lore or the scripture rightly composed by the sages — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: ātmajāṃ rūpasaṃpannāṃ mahatīṃ sadṛśe vare na prayacchati yaḥ kanyāṃ taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who does not bestow his own daughter, endowed with beauty and grown to maturity, upon a worthy suitor — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: adharmanirato mūḍho mithyā yo vai dvijātiṣu dadyān marmātigaṃ śokaṃ taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: The deluded man, devoted to unrighteousness, who falsely inflicts upon the twice-born a grief that pierces to the quick — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā viprahīnasya paṅgulasya jaḍasya vā hareta yo vai sarvasvaṃ taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who carries off the whole property of one bereft of sight, of a cripple, or of a simpleton — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: āśrame vā vane vā yo grāme vā yadi vā pure agniṃ samutsṛjen mohāt taṃ vidyād brahmaghātinam
english: He who in his folly sets loose fire upon a hermitage, a forest, a village, or a town — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tīrthānāṃ darśanaṃ śreyaḥ snānaṃ ca bharatarṣabha śravaṇaṃ ca mahāprājña śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The sight of the sacred fords is a blessing, and bathing in them too, O bull of the Bharatas; and hearing of them as well, O greatly wise one — I wish to hear of them truly.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni puṇyāni bharatarṣabha vaktum arhasi me tāni śrotāsmi niyataḥ prabho
english: Those holy fords that are upon the earth, O bull of the Bharatas, you ought to tell me of them; I shall listen, intent and self-restrained, O lord.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca imam aṅgirasā proktaṃ tīrthavaṃśaṃ mahādyute śrotum arhasi bhadraṃ te prāpsyase dharmam uttamam
english: Bhīṣma said: This lineage of the sacred fords, declared by Aṅgiras, O one of great splendor, you ought to hear — blessings be upon you; you shall attain the highest dharma.

sanskrit: tapovanagataṃ vipram abhigamya mahāmunim papracchāṅgirasaṃ vīra gautamaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Approaching the brāhmaṇa, the great sage Aṅgiras, who had gone to the grove of austerities, Gautama of rigid vows questioned him, O hero.

sanskrit: asti me bhagavan kaś cit tīrthebhyo dharmasaṃśayaḥ tat sarvaṃ śrotum icchāmi tan me śaṃsa mahāmune
english: I have, O blessed one, a certain doubt concerning the dharma of the sacred fords. All of it I wish to hear; declare it to me, O great sage.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya phalaṃ kiṃ syāt teṣu tīrtheṣu vai mune pretyabhāve mahāprājña tad yathāsti tathā vada
english: What fruit accrues from touching the waters at those fords, O sage, in the life beyond, O greatly wise one? Tell it to me just as it is.

sanskrit: aṅgirā uvāca saptāhaṃ candrabhāgāṃ vai vitastām ūrmimālinīm vigāhya vai nirāhāro nirmamo munivad bhavet
english: Aṅgiras said: He who for seven days plunges into the Candrabhāgā and the wave-garlanded Vitastā, fasting and free of all sense of possession, becomes like unto a sage.

sanskrit: kāśmīramaṇḍale nadyo yāḥ patanti mahānadam tā nadīḥ sindhum āsādya śīlavān svargam āpnuyāt
english: The rivers that, in the region of Kāśmīra, fall into the great river — coming to those streams of the Sindhu, the man of virtuous conduct attains heaven.

sanskrit: puṣkaraṃ ca prabhāsaṃ ca naimiṣaṃ sāgarodakam devikām indramārgaṃ ca svarṇabinduṃ vigāhya ca vibodhyate vimānasthaḥ so 'psarobhir abhiṣṭutaḥ
english: Having plunged into Puṣkara, Prabhāsa, Naimiṣa, the ocean-waters, the Devikā, the Indramārga, and the Svarṇabindu, a man is awakened set upon a celestial chariot, hymned by the apsarases.

sanskrit: hiraṇyabinduṃ vikṣobhya prayataś cābhivādya tam kuśeśayaṃ ca devatvaṃ pūyate tasya kilbiṣam
english: Having stirred the waters of Hiraṇyabindu and, self-controlled, reverently saluted the Kuśeśaya, he attains godhead, and his sin is washed away.

sanskrit: indratoyāṃ samāsādya gandhamādanasaṃnidhau karatoyāṃ kuraṅgeṣu trirātropoṣito naraḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti vigāhya niyataḥ śuciḥ
english: Reaching the Indratoyā near Gandhamādana, and the Karatoyā among the Kuraṅgas, the man who has fasted three nights and plunges in, restrained and pure, gains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: gaṅgādvāre kuśāvarte bilvake nemiparvate tathā kanakhale snātvā dhūtapāpmā divaṃ vrajet
english: Having bathed at the Gate of the Gaṅgā, at Kuśāvarta, at Bilvaka, at Mount Nemi, and at Kanakhala, a man, his sins shaken off, goes to heaven.

sanskrit: apāṃ hrada upaspṛśya vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet brahmacārī jitakrodhaḥ satyasaṃdhas tv ahiṃsakaḥ
english: Touching the waters at the lake Apāṃ Hrada, a chaste man who has conquered wrath, true to his word and harmless to all, gains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: yatra bhāgīrathī gaṅgā bhajate diśam uttarām maheśvarasya niṣṭhāne yo naras tv abhiṣicyate ekamāsaṃ nirāhāraḥ svayaṃ paśyati devatāḥ
english: Where the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā turns toward the northern quarter, at the abode of Maheśvara, the man who is consecrated there, fasting for a whole month, beholds the gods themselves.

sanskrit: saptagaṅge trigaṅge ca indramārge ca tarpayan sudhāṃ vai labhate bhoktuṃ yo naro jāyate punaḥ
english: At Saptagaṅga, at Trigaṅga, and at the Indramārga, the man who offers libations to the fathers gains the nectar of immortality to taste, when he is born again.

sanskrit: mahāśrama upaspṛśya yo 'gnihotraparaḥ śuciḥ ekamāsaṃ nirāhāraḥ siddhiṃ māsena sa vrajet
english: Touching the waters at Mahāśrama, the pure man devoted to the fire-offering, fasting for a whole month, attains perfection in that month.

sanskrit: mahāhrada upaspṛśya bhṛgutuṅge tv alolupaḥ trirātropoṣito bhūtvā mucyate brahmahatyayā
english: Touching the waters at the Great Lake on Bhṛgutuṅga, the man free of greed, having fasted three nights, is released from the guilt of brahmin-murder.

sanskrit: kanyākūpa upaspṛśya balākāyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ deveṣu kīrtiṃ labhate yaśasā ca virājate
english: Touching the waters at the Kanyākūpa and making his offering of water in the Balākā, a man wins renown among the gods and shines forth in glory.

sanskrit: deśakāla upaspṛśya tathā sundarikāhrade aśvibhyāṃ rūpavarcasyaṃ pretya vai labhate naraḥ
english: Touching the waters at Deśakāla and likewise in the lake Sundarikā, a man gains from the Aśvins beauty and brilliance of form when he passes to the other world.

sanskrit: mahāgaṅgām upaspṛśya kṛttikāṅgārake tathā pakṣam ekaṃ nirāhāraḥ svargam āpnoti nirmalaḥ
english: Touching the waters of the Mahāgaṅgā, and likewise at Kṛttikā and Aṅgāraka, a man who fasts for a single fortnight, made spotless, attains heaven.

sanskrit: vaimānika upaspṛśya kiṅkiṇīkāśrame tathā nivāse 'psarasāṃ divye kāmacārī mahīyate
english: Touching the waters at Vaimānika and likewise at the hermitage of Kiṅkiṇīkā, in the celestial dwelling of the apsarases, a man is honored and roams there at will.

sanskrit: kālikāśramam āsādya vipāśāyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ brahmacārī jitakrodhas trirātrān mucyate bhavāt
english: Reaching the hermitage of Kālikā and making his offering of water in the Vipāśā, a chaste man who has conquered wrath is freed, after three nights, from the round of rebirth.

sanskrit: āśrame kṛttikānāṃ tu snātvā yas tarpayet pitṝn toṣayitvā mahādevaṃ nirmalaḥ svargam āpnuyāt
english: He who bathes at the hermitage of the Kṛttikās and offers libations to the fathers, having gladdened Mahādeva, made spotless, attains heaven.

sanskrit: mahāpura upaspṛśya trirātropoṣito naraḥ trasānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca dvipadānāṃ bhayaṃ tyajet
english: Touching the waters at Mahāpura, a man who has fasted three nights casts off all fear of moving creatures, of unmoving things, and of men.

sanskrit: devadāruvane snātvā dhūtapāpmā kṛtodakaḥ devalokam avāpnoti saptarātroṣitaḥ śuciḥ
english: Having bathed in the Devadāru grove, his sins shaken off, and made his offering of water, the pure man who has fasted seven nights attains the world of the gods.

sanskrit: kauśante ca kuśastambe droṇaśarmapade tathā āpaḥprapatane snātaḥ sevyate so 'psarogaṇaiḥ
english: At Kauśanta, at Kuśastamba, at Droṇaśarmapada, and bathing at Āpaḥprapatana, a man is waited upon by the throngs of apsarases.

sanskrit: citrakūṭe janasthāne tathā mandākinījale vigāhya vai nirāhāro rājalakṣmīṃ nigacchati
english: Plunging, while fasting, into Citrakūṭa, into Janasthāna, and into the waters of the Mandākinī, a man attains the royal fortune of a king.

sanskrit: śyāmāyās tv āśramaṃ gatvā uṣya caivābhiṣicya ca trīṃs trirātrān sa saṃdhāya gandharvanagare vaset
english: Having gone to the hermitage of Śyāmā, and dwelling there and bathing, after spending three sets of three nights in succession, a man may dwell in the city of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: ramaṇyāṃ ca upaspṛśya tathā vai gandhatārike ekamāsaṃ nirāhāras tv antardhānaphalaṃ labhet
english: Touching the waters at Ramaṇyā and likewise at Gandhatārikā, a man who fasts for a whole month gains the power of vanishing from sight.

sanskrit: kauśikīdvāram āsādya vāyubhakṣas tv alolupaḥ ekaviṃśatirātreṇa svargam ārohate naraḥ
english: Reaching the Gate of the Kauśikī, a man free of greed who feeds on air alone ascends to heaven after twenty-one nights.
